grade_rationale.text: Machal records the Poludnica for the Czechs of Bohemia and Moravia, the Poles, the Lusatian Serbs and the Russians, including the Siberian Russians.
Afanasyev records the poludnitsa in southern Siberia and Archangel Government, among the Lusatians, and among the Czechs.
Machal's field-spirit pages 267-268 cite no source, so nothing on them shows dependence on Afanasyev; Machal and Afanasyev count as two independent sources.
Ralston's Lusatian account closely matches Afanasyev's, and the same passage cites "Afanasief, P. V. S. iii. 77" in its footnotes, so Ralston is not counted as independent of Afanasyev.
Erben's prose note gives Czech folk belief about the poludnice, but Erben is a literary source and is not counted as collected folklore; the grade does not rest on him.
